title: Ordinary reduction squares for forward structural isomorphisms
statement: Fix l,E,o and normalized ambient models a [def-sf-integral-realization-assembly-data], an arbitrary scheme B, family X:I→Over B and ordinary integral inputs K. If the independently specified system and ringed isomorphisms s:e_system(RK)≅t_system(RK) and r:e_ringed(K)≅t_ringed(K) form a CanonicalIsoPair [def-sf-integral-system-realization-data], then rho_e followed by s.hom equals R(r.hom) followed by rho_t, where rho is the explicit ordinary coefficient recursion [def-sf-integral-ordinary-expression-reduction]. Only the listed forward isomorphism generators are covered. There is no realization comparison, completion transport, BasicPair unit/counit or arbitrary outer context in the assertion.

source.place: The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits, whose coefficient comparisons are proved in lem-fix-operation-reduction; coherence inherited from individual maps.

proof.text: Case split on the nine constructors of CanonicalIsoPair. For pull composition use canonicalReductionPullComposition and naturality in the child coefficient map. Apply mate_compositor_square to its inverse-component equation for proper composition; naturality again inserts the child map.

Tensor reassociation follows from comparison_associator, which derives associativity from reduction_compatible and transports across tensorClosed. It allows arbitrary three child coefficient maps, including repeated inputs.
For tensor/pullback use the primitive two-object coefficient square, and naturality of the system tensor/pullback comparison to insert both child coefficient maps.

The fixed open reduction mate is invertible at every ordinary input. For open composition, apply injectivity of mateEquiv to the composition square and use canonical pull composition; invert this equality and use compositor naturality. For cartesian open base change, transpose the inverse comparison under the open adjunction. Substitute the given beta_transpose fields. Paste the open-unit square with the pullback square, obtained from two pull compositors and equality transport. This proves the inverse coefficient square; cancellation of the two structural isomorphisms gives the forward square. For the clopen comparison, transpose under the direct-image adjunction and cancel the invertible open units; the open-unit square and direct counit mate square give the required equality.

For open projection transpose its inverse under the open adjunction. Substitute projection_transpose on both sides, factor the tensor of the open-unit square and the second pullback coefficient map, and apply tensor-reduction naturality. The inverse primitive tensor/pullback coefficient square and pullback/tensor naturality identify the remaining factors. Invert the resulting structural square. This argument uses no completion or arbitrary realization comparisons.
Compactification expansion has identity structural arrows and identical open-then-proper ordinary reduction recursions; simplification of identities and reflexivity close this case.

proof_origin.place: The individual-map coefficient sentence, using formal mate calculus for all open cases and one primitive two-object pullback/tensor coefficient square; B5.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryCanonicalIsoSquare
    (o : Operations l E) (a : AmbientModels l E o)
    {B : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} {X : I → Over B}
    (K : ∀ i, Integral l E (X i).left)
    {W : Over B} (e t : Expression B I X W)
    (s : e.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K) ≅
      t.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K))
    (r : e.ringedObj l E a.ringedModels K ≅ t.ringedObj l E a.ringedModels K)
    (h : CanonicalIsoPair l E o a.compositors a.openComparisons a.ringedModels
      a.ringedOpenComparisons ((inputReduction l E X).obj K) K e t s r) :
    e.ordinaryReduction l E o a K ≫ s.hom =
      (calculus l E W.left).reduction.map r.hom ≫ t.ordinaryReduction l E o a K
